فهم المقروء:
A queue that moves steadily feels shorter than a queue of the same length that stops and starts, even when the wait is identical. Research on waiting has produced a set of findings that are consistent enough to design around. Unoccupied time feels longer than occupied time, which is why mirrors near lifts and information screens in stations reduce complaints without reducing the wait. Uncertain waits feel longer than known ones: a sign saying the next train arrives in nine minutes is more tolerable than no sign at all, even when nine minutes is the longer wait. Unexplained waits feel longest of all, and an announcement giving a reason reliably lowers irritation. And people tolerate a long wait for something they value far better than a short wait for something they do not. None of this shortens anything.
